newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's FCL Bldg sees positive infrastructure outlook.
newsitem.headline: NZ's FCL Bldg sees positive infrastructure outlook.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Building Ltd said on Wednesday the domestic outlook was generally positive for construction but the regional wood panels markets remained in over-supply.
Commercial and infrastructure sectors were expected to provide strong demand while the residential market would soften in 1998, FCL Building said.

"Over the past six months, demand in the residential sector in New Zealand has softened as a result of a steep decline in immigration and lower consumer confidence," chief executive Terry McFadgen told a news conference.
"Provided consumer confidence lifts, we expect demand in the sector to recover over the 1998 calendar year," he said.
The wood panels operation was breaking even at the pre-interest, pre-tax level.

"However, further improvement will be largely dependent on regional medium density fibreboard (MDF) prices," McFadgen said. In the commercial and infrastructure sectors, FCL Building expected strong demand to continue, buoyed by a large number of projects in the roading, transport, waste disposal, schools and hospital sectors, many of which were at an early stage of implementation. In Auckland, there were projects worth NZ$1 in train.
McFadgen said Building's earnings, at the pre-tax level, should materially exceed those of 1996/97.

"Beyond the next 12 months, FCL Building remains uniquely placed to benefit from the significant backlog of infrastructure needs in New Zealand," he said. --Wellington newsroom (64 4) 473 4746; Fax (64 4) 473 6212
